title: CONSER & BIBCO Standard Records
summary: Guidelines for subject headings on CONSER Standard Records (CSR) and BIBCO Standard Records (BSR). Assign at least one or two headings for the primary/essential subject and/or form at the appropriate specificity, generally matching the class number; secondary topics are normally omitted. Multiple headings may be needed for compound topics, reciprocal pairs, and prescribed arrays. Music recordings get one to three headings. GACs follow Appendix E.
validation_rules: On BSR/CSR records assign at least one or two headings representing the primary subject and/or form at the appropriate level of specificity, generally corresponding to the class number. (H 170 sec. 1)
Secondary or tertiary subjects are normally not represented on standard records, even if they constitute 20% or more of the item. (H 170 sec. 1)

Reciprocal headings are assigned in pairs, e.g. `[place 1]--Foreign relations--[place 2]` and `[place 2]--Foreign relations--[place 1]`; prescribed arrays (e.g. biographies, H 1330) are assigned in full. (H 170 sec. 1)
Subdivide by topical, geographic, chronological, and/or form subdivisions as appropriate for the primary subject (H 180 sec. 16). (H 170 sec. 1)
Music recordings on standard records receive one to three subject headings; for more than three works use one to three broader headings if no essential information is lost. (H 170 sec. 2)
Assign GACs (043) per Appendix E. (H 170 sec. 3)

sections.heading: 1. General guidelines
sections.text:
If appropriate, assign at least one or two headings from the subject authority file and/or the name authority file to represent the primary subject and/or form of the work at the appropriate level of specificity. Assign headings to provide access to the essential subject focus of the work. This focus should generally correspond to the meaning of the assigned class number.

Concentrating on the primary or essential subject focus of a work means that secondary or tertiary subjects will normally not be represented in the assigned subject headings of a standard record, even if they constitute at least 20% of an item (cf. H 180 sec. 1). Multiple headings may be needed to represent a compound or multi-element topic for which a single heading neither exists nor can practically be constructed or established (cf. H 180 sec. 10). Multiple headings may also be needed in situations where reciprocal headings are used, for example, [place 1]--Foreign relations--[place 2] and [place 2]--Foreign relations--[place 1], or where a standard array of headings is prescribed, for example, on biographies (cf. H 1330).

Where appropriate, subdivide main headings by topical, geographic, chronological, and/or form subdivisions to bring out those aspects of the primary subject (cf. H 180 sec. 16).

Assign headings at the level of specificity appropriate to the work (cf. H 180 sec. 4). Establish new headings for discrete topics and named entities as they are needed.

sections.heading: 2. Music recordings
sections.text: Assign from the subject authority file one to three subject headings at the appropriate level of specificity. A recording of three major classical works, for example, may receive up to three headings. If more than three works are involved, assign one to three broader headings as necessary if no essential information will be lost. Otherwise, assign the minimum number of headings necessary to provide essential information.

sections.heading: 3. Geographic area codes or GACs (043)
sections.text: Assign geographic area codes following the instructions in Appendix E.
